A generated project stays intentionally small. Your TSX runs in a Bun worker while QuickGUI keeps the platform event loop on the native main thread.

## Generated files

```text
my-app/
├── src/
│   └── app.tsx
├── package.json
├── quickgui.config.ts
└── tsconfig.json
```

Put application UI in `src/`. Add files and directories to production bundles through the `resources` option.

## Application entry

The entry module waits for the native app, creates windows, and passes a Solid root to `createRenderer`.

```tsx
await app.whenReady();

new Window({
  title: "Notes",
  renderer: createRenderer(() => <NotesApp />),
});
```

Source modules may use ordinary Bun APIs. Keep native application and window work asynchronous at the hosted boundary.

## Configuration

`quickgui.config.ts` tells the CLI what to compile and package.

```tsx
import { defineConfig } from "@quickgui/cli";

export default defineConfig({
  entry: "src/app.tsx",
  productName: "Notes",
  identifier: "dev.example.notes",
  resources: ["assets"],
});
```

Release-only options cover icons, signing, notarization, the Mac App Store, and updater manifests.

## Packages

| Package | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `@quickgui/native` | Application, windows, menus, dialogs, notifications, and native services |
| `@quickgui/solid` | Solid renderer, primitives, components, and routing |
| `@quickgui/solid/swift-ui` | Native SwiftUI controls hosted from Solid on macOS |
| `@quickgui/cli` | Project creation, development, and production packaging |
